correctness.rationale: For every prime power \(q\), positive dimension and nested flag, the strictly increasing number of proper subspaces recovers ambient subspace rank in the first round. First-round atom colours also record membership in each marked flag subspace. Second-round counts of predecessor atoms from these classes yield exactly \((q^{\dim(W\cap U_i)}-1)/(q-1)\), uniquely recovering every intersection dimension (rank-zero and rank-one exceptions are handled directly). A flag-adapted basis maps any two subspaces with the same intersection-dimension sequence by a flag-preserving linear automorphism, so the partition is not over-refined. Successive graph-of-linear-map lifts prove the cardinality formula. Two independent programs reproduce this classification for selected small finite-field examples, with explicit binary general-linear stabilizer actions; the infinite theorem is based on the proof, not the sampling. The \(\mathbb F_2^4\) two-plane witness proves sharpness.

value.rationale: The flag-stabilizer orbit problem is natural in finite projective geometry and descriptive complexity. The theorem gives a complete orbit invariant for an unbounded, non-distributive lattice family, identifies every class within a field-size- and dimension-independent two-round logical bound, and recovers the exact Gaussian cell-size profile. The q-independent class count together with a sharp one-versus-two-round witness makes this more than a numerical recomputation of known Schubert cells. Such an exact structural benchmark can inform comparisons with cover-graph refinement, nonnested marks and higher-arity counting logics. No downstream theorem is required for its direct mathematical value.
